column1: # lean-overrides.tsv — the PERSISTENT operator-override register (#613).
# Read by plugins/dev-pipeline/tools/operator-override.sh and validated at the merge boundary.
# Almost every override belongs in the per-issue record instead
# (<plansDir>/<slug>-<issue>-lean-override.md, written by that tool's `record`); a row here is
# for the rare class that must outlive one run.
# WHY THIS FILE IS SAFE WHERE AN APPEND-PER-RUN REGISTER IS NOT: a central file every run touches
# conflicts by construction. Persistent overrides are rare by design, so this one is edited about
# as often as scripts/fail-open-sites.tsv — and, like that file, it is hand-edited and argued
# about in a PR rather than written by a tool. There is no `add` verb on purpose.
# TAB-separated. Columns:
#   gate <TAB> scope <TAB> region <TAB> expiry <TAB> justification
# gate           intake-unqueued | spec-open-region  (the closed consumer enum)
# scope          intake-attestation | open-region-resolution  (the authority scope, never an identity)
# region         OR-n for the region-scoped gate; `none` otherwise.
# expiry         The single form `until-issue:<N>` — a CONDITION, not a clock. A date would
#                import the `date` arithmetic the token design declined, and would expire at
#                midnight rather than when the work it waits on lands. The row is expired the
#                moment issue N closes, and an expired row reds the next run that consults it.
# justification  Why this override must outlive one run. Empty reds.
# No rows today: every override recorded so far has been per-run.
